headerDisplay: Exposes your Read Your Meter Pro water meter in HomeKit. HomeKit has no water-consumption service, so readings are surfaced as **light sensors** (the number is your consumption, the unit says "lux" — ignore it) and thresholds as **leak sensors** you can use for automations and notifications.
footerDisplay: For verbose logs, enable Homebridge debug mode (or the debug toggle on this plugin's child bridge). Unofficial; not affiliated with Arad Group or any water corporation.

email.title: Email
email.description: The email address you use to sign in at rym-pro.com.

pollInterval.title: Poll interval (minutes)
pollInterval.description: The meter itself only reports hourly at best, so there is nothing to gain below 60.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: Litres read better in the Home app: 734 instead of 0.734.

weeklyWindow.title: Weekly total covers
weeklyWindow.description: Only affects the weekly sensor and its alert. A calendar week resets on its start day, so early in the week the total is small — and since the portal publishes a day late, it can show nothing at all for a day or two after the reset, where it holds last week's figure instead. The rolling option never resets: it is always the seven days ending today, which makes it steadier to compare and to set an alert on, but it is not "this week" and it will not go back down after a heavy week until those days age out.

dailyThreshold.title: Daily alert threshold
dailyThreshold.description: Trips the daily alert when the latest published day's consumption reaches this value, in the unit selected above. Note the portal publishes a day's figure a day or two late, so this is a budget alarm on a completed day, not a live one. A rough starting point is 400 litres per person per day — roughly double a normal day, so it flags a genuine problem rather than a long shower. Watch the plugin's debug log for a week and adjust. 0 removes the sensor.

weeklyThreshold.title: Weekly alert threshold
weeklyThreshold.description: Trips the weekly alert when the weekly consumption reaches this value. Which week that is — this calendar week, or the last 7 days — is set by "Weekly total covers" under Advanced, and the total is missing whichever recent days the portal has not published yet, so treat it as a floor. 0 removes the sensor.

monthlyThreshold.title: Monthly alert threshold
monthlyThreshold.description: Trips the monthly alert when this month's consumption reaches this value. 3500 litres per person per month is the subsidised household allocation in Israel, so that is a useful place to put it: the alert then means "from here on the water costs about double". 0 removes the sensor.

exposeDaily.title: Latest daily consumption
exposeDaily.description: The most recent day the portal has published — often not today, since figures land a day or two late.

exposeWeekly.title: This week's consumption
exposeWeekly.description: Either the current calendar week so far or the last 7 days, per "Weekly total covers" under Advanced. Summed from the daily figures already fetched, so it costs no extra requests.

exposeForecast.title: Month-end forecast
exposeForecast.description: The portal's own estimate of what this whole calendar month will add up to. Comparable to the monthly threshold.

exposeTotal.title: Cumulative meter reading
exposeTotal.description: Always reported in m³, since a lifetime total in litres exceeds HomeKit's 100000 ceiling.

layout.title: Sensors
layout.description: Switching a sensor off removes it from HomeKit on the next restart. The three alert sensors are controlled by their thresholds above: 0 removes them.

layout.title: Names
layout.description: Leave these empty to name the sensors in the Home app instead — renames there are remembered across restarts. Filling one in pins the name, and a rename in the Home app will be undone on the next restart. HomeKit only accepts names that start and end with a letter or digit.
